race.name: L'Etape Italy Piemonte by Tour de France
race.display_name: L'Etape Italy Piemonte by Tour de France
race.tagline: Competitive Maritime Alps gran fondo: 140 km, 2,821 meters, and a steep gravel pass

vitals.start_format: Gridded mass start; gun-time finish classification with the Colle delle Goderie gravel descent neutralized
vitals.registration: 2026 registration closed; no 2027 registration cycle published
vitals.entry_fee: €50 early / €75 after April 30 (2026 competitive race); €25 applied only to the separate family ride
vitals.feed_zones: 2026: km 54.4 Festiona, km 83.1 Vernante, km 89.2 Colle delle Goderie, km 120.5 Festiona
vitals.cutoff_time: 15:00 at the Gran Fondo/Medio route split; later riders were directed onto the Medio course
route_options: Granfondo: current route page 140.12 km / 2,821 m; formal 2026 regulations and FAQ list 144.9 km / 2,894 m
Mediofondo: current route page 110 km / 2,101 m; formal 2026 regulations and FAQ list 114.8 km / 2,184 m
Cicloturistica: separate noncompetitive family ride, current route page 55.71 km / 815 m

climate.description: The race crosses three Maritime Alps valleys in late May. The organizer does not publish a fixed weather range, so use the current forecast and participant briefing rather than a historical temperature assumption.
challenges: Weather exposure across the Gesso, Stura, and Vermenagna valleys
Layering for long climbs and the neutralized Goderie descent

terrain.primary: Maritime Alps roads with three major climbs and a summit gravel sector
terrain.surface: Mostly paved mountain roads. Colle delle Goderie climbs 6.1 km at 9.4% average, beginning on asphalt before a gravel sector; its gravel descent was neutralized until the route returned to asphalt.
features: Madonna del Colletto climbed from both sides on the long route
Colle delle Goderie: 6.1 km at 9.4% average
A gravel sector near the Goderie summit and a neutralized gravel descent
Gun-time overall classification plus timed jersey competitions

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Corrected 2026-08-08 from the organizer's regulations, route page, FAQ, and participant briefing. The old profile described only the separate 50 km family ride and incorrectly called the event noncompetitive. The 2026 Gran Fondo was a gun-time competitive race on a roughly 140 km / 2,821 m course, with a roughly 110 km Medio option, official classifications, category awards, and timed jersey competitions. Distance 2->3, climbing 2->4, descent technicality 2->3, community culture 5->4, and field depth 2->3. Score 63->69; tier remains T2.

key_climbs.name: Madonna del Colletto
key_climbs.description: Climbed from both sides on the Gran Fondo route and once from Valdieri on the Medio route.

key_climbs.name: Colle delle Goderie
key_climbs.description: The polka-dot jersey climb, with a steep paved opening and a gravel sector before a neutralized gravel descent.

climb_profile.profile_type: Three-climb alpine gran fondo with a mixed-surface summit sector

course_description.character: The competitive Gran Fondo starts and finishes in Entracque and crosses the Gesso, Stura, and Vermenagna valleys. The long route tackles three major climbs, including both sides of Madonna del Colletto and the new Colle delle Goderie. Most of the course is paved, but Goderie finishes with gravel; the organizer removed the gravel descent time from the overall result until riders returned to asphalt.
course_description.signature_challenge: Colle delle Goderie: 6.1 km at 9.4% average, with steep asphalt followed by gravel and a polka-dot jersey competition near the summit.
suffering_zones: The first Madonna del Colletto ascent from Valdieri
Colle delle Goderie at km 89.2, after two earlier feed zones and before its neutralized gravel descent
The second side of Madonna del Colletto on the long-route return

logistics.airport: The organizer does not name a preferred airport. Its official road directions route drivers via the A6 Turin-Savona and A33 Asti-Cuneo motorways, then Borgo San Dalmazzo, Valdieri, and Entracque.
logistics.lodging_strategy: The organizer offered territory accommodation packages through OM Cycling Tour. Verify the next edition before booking in or around Entracque.
logistics.transport: The 2026 start and finish were on Viale J. F. Kennedy in Entracque; use the next-edition participant briefing for parking and village access.
logistics.food: Four on-course feed zones, a pasta/hamburger party, and a Sunday gala dinner were published for 2026.

history.origin_story: L'Étape Piemonte debuted in Entracque in 2026 as one of two Italian L'Étape by Tour de France events that season. It paired a competitive Gran Fondo and Medio Fondo with a separate family ride rather than treating the 50 km route as the flagship event.
notable_moments: Inaugural 2026 debut in Piemonte's Maritime Alps
First competitive ascent of Colle delle Goderie, used for the polka-dot jersey
The gravel descent from Goderie was neutralized and excluded from total race time
Official classifications included overall, age-category, and Tour de France jersey competitions
history.reputation: A first-edition competitive alpine gran fondo carrying the L'Étape brand; it does not yet have the multi-year record of established Italian classics.

biased_opinion.verdict: A real alpine race, not the family ride it was mistaken for
biased_opinion.summary: The competitive L'Étape Piemonte is a substantial first-edition gran fondo: roughly 140 kilometers, 2,821 meters of climbing, three major ascents, official gun-time results, and a 6.1-kilometer climb averaging 9.4% that changes from asphalt to gravel. The organizer also ran a short family ride, which is what the old profile accidentally described. The race's main uncertainty is continuity, not difficulty: its 2026 debut is complete and no 2027 date or route has been announced.
strengths: A legitimate 140-kilometer competitive course with nearly 2,900 meters of climbing
Colle delle Goderie adds a distinctive steep gravel-topped climb
Closed roads, chip timing, feed zones, and official classifications
Tour de France jersey competitions add clear race targets
The separate Medio Fondo preserves an in-race route choice
weaknesses: Official 2026 pages conflict on final distance and climbing totals
The inaugural race lacks a multi-year execution record
A late 15:00 route split can force slower riders onto the Medio course
The Goderie gravel descent required neutralization
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Treat L'Étape Piemonte as a serious mixed-surface alpine gran fondo once the organizer publishes a next edition. Do not plan against the completed 2026 date.

final_verdict.one_liner: A serious Maritime Alps debut with real climbing, official competition, and a memorable gravel-topped pass.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes when a future edition is officially confirmed if you want a competitive Tour-branded alpine gran fondo with substantial climbing and a controlled mixed-surface sector. Wait to book or train until the organizer publishes the next date and route.
final_verdict.alternatives: Consider Gran Fondo La Fausto Coppi for an established Cuneo alpine classic or L'Étape Mondovì for the other current Piedmont L'Étape event.

eligibility.note: The organizer's formal rules explicitly define the May 31, 2026 Gran Fondo and Medio Fondo as competitive, with gun-time results, classifications, and jersey competitions. The separate roughly 50-kilometer Cicloturistica was the noncompetitive family ride. The 2026 race is complete; no official 2027 date, registration cycle, regulations, or route has been published.
